PullRequest.Title: Improve sandbox dependency warnings and disable action
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Cherry-picks https://github.com/dileepyavan/vscode/commit/33c9fe64718ce7aad4932e7141ccf0e9c02a3b99 onto current `main`.

- Show concise, capability-specific sandbox dependency warnings while retaining detailed runtime diagnostics in logs.
- Add troubleshooting and policy-aware sandbox-disable links for settings and sessions.
- Update sandbox diagnostics, session, and notification regression tests.

The cherry-pick includes adaptations to the current main-branch context and the repository formatter's required test formatting. No changes from the separate sandbox-path-grant work were included.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed after refreshing dependencies to match the updated main branch.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\copilotSandboxDiagnostics.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSandboxDiagnostics.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\agentHostSandboxNotification.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostSandboxNotification.test.ts` — passed, 5 files checked.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSandboxDiagnostics.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostSandboxNotification.test.ts --grep "[Ss]andbox" --reporter dot` — passed, 140 tests.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene — passed; commit signing retained.

Full type-check, integration tests, and live UI validation were not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or resuming a Copilot agent session, and preparing each turn, when sandbox dependencies or capabilities are unavailable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing sandbox host-support RPC is awaited during session initialization and after the existing sandbox configuration RPC during turn preparation. The diff adds synchronous warning-log calls before publishing diagnostics metadata, but does not add or move the RPC onto this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per diagnostics update: session initialization, each sandbox application before a turn, and relevant configuration changes; effective cardinality and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same diagnostics update called and awaited getHostSupport with the same timeout and frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on initialization and turn preparation; timeout is 5 seconds. This boundary was already on those critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Warning logging for an unavailable backend or each relevant missing capability
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One warning for an unsupported backend, or at most the small SDK capability set per failed support result, repeated on each diagnostics query while the condition persists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Technical support reasons were published as session metadata without warning-log calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous log method invocation occurs after the RPC and before metadata publication; downstream log persistence is implementation-managed. The added work is bounded to short messages and a small capability set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of initialized sessions, turns, relevant sandbox configuration updates, and missing capabilities. Capability cardinality is a small fixed SDK set; updates are serialized on turn/config paths and stale diagnostics responses are generation-checked.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turn and configuration sandbox applications use the existing sandbox-config sequencer; diagnostics also rejects stale generations. Sessions can operate independently, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host-support results are not cached before or after the diff. Session diagnostic metadata is still equality-deduplicated; the new technical warning logs are not deduplicated, but their bounded per-turn volume is insufficient to establish a user-visible performance regression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call frequency and added logging because all update call sites and turn/config sequencing were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual log sink cost varies by host, but only one to a few short records are added per explicit diagnostics update; no evidence shows meaningful latency, throughput, or I/O degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: RPC cardinality and critical-path placement are unchanged, and the only new repeated work is a bounded number of short diagnostic log records.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying and updating the session-scoped sandbox warning as session state, configuration, or managed policy changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session and policy events synchronously compute distinct reasons, inspect in-memory configuration policy, and update the chat input notification only when reasons or disable eligibility change. This is UI update work, but no layout read, network, filesystem, IPC, or subprocess boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously active/open Agent Host chat sessions and session/policy events. Each active session owns one notification object; disposal removes its command and listeners.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates run synchronously per event. Equality checks suppress notification republishing when diagnostics and eligibility are unchanged; managed-policy observables trigger one autorun per active session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reasons and disable eligibility are cached on each instance for update suppression. Dismissals retain one resource key per dismissed session for the notification-service lifetime, but that lifecycle predates the diff. Command registrations and new listeners are disposed with the active chat session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the creation path, active-session ownership, MutableDisposable replacement, and explicit disposal registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A window may have multiple active chat models, but no evidence indicates unbounded active-session retention or a high-frequency managed-policy event stream.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added policy checks and command registrations are lightweight, update-deduplicated, and lifecycle-bound; the diff also reduces diagnostic Markdown/link parsing to the first concise reason.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clicking Disable Sandboxing from the warning
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command revalidates policy, optionally dispatches one session configuration action, then awaits one global configuration update before command completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionConfigChanged to the resolved agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when the session is already off; otherwise one dispatch per explicit command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no disable action and therefore no session dispatch from this notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued synchronously before the settings update so the active session is disabled as part of the requested action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist/update the global sandbox-enabled configuration value
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update per explicit command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no disable action and therefore no configuration write from this notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the disable command resolves; this is the requested settings mutation, not incidental fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit user command invocations, not session history or diagnostic collection size. One invocation affects one active session plus one global setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No shared burst is created; each click invokes one command. Session dispatch is not awaited, while the configuration update is awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The handler rechecks current session state and policy at invocation time. It skips redundant session dispatch when state/config already indicate off; standard configuration handling owns persistence and propagation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the command handler and resolved connection dispatch path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration persistence latency depends on environment, but cardinality is one and directly required by the user action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: both introduced boundaries are bounded to one explicit user action and are necessary to implement that action; redundant session IPC is suppressed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced initialization/turn diagnostics, warning rendering and lifecycle, managed-policy reactions, and the disable action through RPC, IPC, logging, configuration persistence, caching, and concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
